policy: These are user-provided aliases and public workflow ideas, not native ChatGPT commands or proof of installed features. Each alias maps to a task template; unsupported integrations must remain blocked and clearly labeled.
aliases: Separate facts, user claims, assumptions, estimates and unknowns; identify missing evidence and avoid unsupported completion claims.
Break the task into assumptions, constraints and fundamental truths; derive a practical solution and verify it.
Identify low-probability, high-impact failure modes, leading indicators and reversible mitigations.
Separate high-signal evidence from repetition, hype and low-quality sources; preserve provenance.
Provide scenarios, assumptions, confidence and falsifiable indicators; do not present forecasts as facts.
Return the shortest accurate summary, key caveats and next action.
Explore materially different options, dependencies and second-order effects; return auditable conclusions, not hidden chain-of-thought.
Identify unproductive criticism, retain valid objections, then revise constructively.
Compare safest, fastest and most scalable approaches with cost, risk and reversibility.
Create phased milestones, dependencies, owners, acceptance tests and rollback criteria.
List only tools available to this runtime, their permissions and verification status; do not infer installation.
Inventory user-owned prompts and documented presets; do not claim access to private system prompts.
Distinguish actual platform features, user-defined aliases and unsupported commands.
Write naturally for the target audience without invented personal experience or manipulative pressure.
Probe assumptions, abuse cases, data exposure, permission boundaries and failure modes.
Explain in plain language with an example and an important caveat.
Use structured analysis and return key rationale, alternatives and verifiable steps.
Review the decision at one, three and five years; identify lock-in and maintenance risks.
Decompose systems into components, inputs, outputs, dependencies, owners and tests.
Expose hidden assumptions, missing dependencies, edge cases and failure paths.
Prepare content for a handwritten-style visual only when an authorized image tool is available.
Split ideas into small labeled cards with status and next action.
Construct the strongest fair version of each side before evaluating evidence.
Challenge the proposal with its strongest objections and observable disconfirming evidence.
Generate playful, unconventional ideas, then screen for feasibility and safety.
Create audience-specific messaging, hooks and ethical experiments; do not promise virality.
Convert a goal into a repeatable SOP with controls, checkpoints and escalation.
Produce original content from sourced research with rights, fact-check and review metadata.
Build age-appropriate learning content with source references, learning objectives and assessment.
Create truthful sales enablement with qualification, value proposition and compliance checks.
Create a simple visual brief or diagram specification with accessible labels.
Adjust tone, rhythm and cultural nuance without changing factual meaning.
Map trigger, inputs, decisions, actions, failure paths and measurable outputs.
Generate a high-diversity idea batch, then rank novelty, evidence, cost and risk.
Give ordered steps, prerequisites, expected result and recovery guidance.
Show sources, assumptions, decisions, confidence and unresolved issues.
Draft an anime-inspired explainer brief; use only licensed or original assets.
Create a sourced chronology and flag uncertain dates.
Create a hierarchical concept map with cross-links and unresolved questions.
Prepare a concise visual-reference brief with readable labels and source notes.
Show components separated by function and explain their interfaces.
Review a subject across stakeholder, technical, commercial, ethical and operational perspectives.
Create a compact, accurate reference sheet with caveats.
Define components, contracts, dependencies, security boundaries and acceptance criteria.
Generate question-answer cards from verified source material.
Summarize key points, decisions, risks and next actions.
Explain the plan, rationale, dependencies, owner decisions and acceptance evidence.
Give a representative example and state where it does not generalize.
Explain using an analogy and map the analogy's limits.
Return ordered, actionable steps with prerequisites and checks.
Create an answerable quiz and an answer key grounded in the supplied material.
Generate focused research questions and identify evidence needed.
Create an infographic brief with source notes and accessible hierarchy.
Show events in chronological order with dates and provenance.
Compare options on consistent criteria and disclose missing data.
Score options using explicit criteria, weights and uncertainty.
Use an available editing canvas only if the runtime exposes it; otherwise return editable content.
Separate the system into layers with responsibilities and interfaces.
Represent recurring workflows, feedback and stop conditions.
Create a structured sketchnote brief with short labels and clear hierarchy.
Separate visible symptoms from underlying causes and assumptions.
Define outcome, baseline, metric, deadline, constraints and acceptance.
Create a concise actionable brief with audience, purpose, constraints and evidence.
Create a sequenced plan with owners, dependencies, checks and fallback.
Identify the single highest-value safe next action and perform it if authorized.
Rank work by impact, urgency, dependencies, risk and effort.
Make the priority order explicit and explain trade-offs.
Simplify wording while preserving meaning, evidence and caveats.
Generate diverse ideas and group them by value and effort.
Expand the option set before evaluating feasibility and risk.
Draft truthful audience hooks without deceptive claims or bait.
Tailor job-search materials to real experience and a specific role.
Use an available authorized image-generation tool; otherwise return a prompt and asset brief.
Use available study-mode features if exposed; otherwise guide learning with questions and feedback.
Use an available search connector and cite sources; if unavailable, say so.
Use an available execution environment for calculations; never claim code ran without evidence.
Create a concept-map or visual-learning brief using verified source material.
Generate handwritten-style notes only when the authorized image tool supports it.
Test comprehension and explain incorrect answers.
Summarize supplied content and preserve important caveats.
Translate while preserving meaning, register and cultural context.
Rewrite for the requested tone while preserving factual claims.
Produce a diagram specification or render only with an available visualization tool.
Create slide structure, speaker notes and source references.
